raw_response:
I'm 60 this year, and I've worked these 15 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished senior high school, which wasn't common when I was young, so I can read the extension leaflets and understand what the soil test says. But honestly, after four decades, I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than any pamphlet. My wife and I are the only ones living on the farm now—our children work in Shijiazhuang and send money back, which means we have some cash in hand, but we can't do the heavy labor like we used to. We hire people for harvest, planting, and anything that needs carrying.

I split my land into two parts: 10 mu for wheat-maize double cropping, and 5 mu for cotton. The wheat went in last October—Jimai 22, a solid improved variety. I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base dressing at planting. Now it's late April and the wheat is heading out. I already managed the spring work: irrigated once at green-up in March, then irrigated and topdressed 20 kg of urea per mu at jointing in early April. I'll irrigate one more time at heading if the weather stays dry, and I'll keep an eye out for powdery mildew—my neighbor had trouble with it last year, so I might spray fungicide as a precaution. I expect about 480 kg/mu. I'm not chasing record yields; at my age, steady and manageable is better than risky.

For cotton, I'm planting this week on the 5 mu. I use GK99, a hybrid variety. I'll plow and prepare the beds, then spread 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting. Cotton needs attention—bollworm is always a threat, so I'll spray insecticide three or four times through the season. I'll irrigate at flowering and again at boll-setting. Picking is labor-intensive, but with only 5 mu we can handle it, maybe with some hired help. I'm hoping for 230 kg of lint per mu.

The summer maize follows immediately after wheat harvest in early June. The window is tight—sometimes only three to five days between harvest and planting—so I'll hire a combine for wheat and a mechanized planter for maize. I plant Zhengdan 958, the standard hybrid around here. I'll apply 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then topdress 20 kg of urea at the big trumpet stage in mid-July. One or two irrigations depending on rainfall, and I'll watch for armyworms in August.

All told, seeds, fertilizer, pesticides, irrigation electricity, and hired labor will cost me about 12,000 yuan this year. That's a big outlay, but with my children helping and 40 years of knowing this land, I'm comfortable with it. I'd rather spend a bit more on inputs than risk a bad harvest—at 60, I don't have time to recover from a major loss.
